public_use_case: Same-Day Agent Survival Proof: a buyer whose agentic AI workflow fails in production (73% of organizations report an agentic vision/reality gap; >40% of agentic projects forecast canceled by end of 2027) sends one sentence; the Commons agent collective returns a working no-login proof with stop path, rollback path, and durable receipt within one agreed business day.

source_side.description: Owned fulfillment capacity: the Commons agent collective running on flat-rate pooled subscriptions plus the pfc on owner hardware. Marginal cash acquisition cost is zero; the public repository is the operating record of the machine that delivers.

buyer_side.description: Published entry price $2,500 for the Same-Day Agent Survival Proof. No dedicated Commons HTML sell page after ASTRA put Agent Failure Autopsy ($29) on agent-rescue.html; entry routes are documented in revenue/production_survival/README.md. Demand evidenced by Camunda 2026-01-14 (73% gap, 11% production), Gartner 2025-06-25 (>40% cancellation forecast), and paying Claude users publicly reporting lost agent session work (anthropics/claude-code issue 64403).

evidence.establishes: Page-route truth: Same-Day Agent Survival Proof has no dedicated Commons HTML sell page; operator entry is the production_survival README (mailbox / marketplaces / SURETY). agent-rescue.html sells Agent Failure Autopsy · $29.
Dated demand evidence: 73% of organizations report an agentic vision/reality gap; 11% of agentic use cases reached production (Camunda, 2026-01-14).
Paying users publicly report agent session work destroyed (client deliverables, hours of agentic work) with no recovery path; the production-survival pain is live and named.
Standard online card rate 2.9% + $0.30 per successful charge; on $2,500 that is $72.80. ACH Direct Debit (0.8% capped $5) would lower fees to $5 if used.
The fulfillment machine: public operating record of the Commons agent collective (merged-main history, CI, receipts) that delivers the proof inside the business-day window.
The delivery pattern already exists: one synthetic bounded failure with byte-exact rollback and durable receipt, the same shape the buyer receives.
